Class Grid

java.lang.Object
javafx.scene.Node
javafx.scene.Parent
javafx.scene.layout.Region
javafx.scene.control.Control
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.Grid
All Implemented Interfaces:
javafx.css.Styleable, javafx.event.EventTarget, javafx.scene.control.Skinnable
Direct Known Subclasses:
TreeGrid
public class Grid extends javafx.scene.control.Control

A table that paints all cells into one canvas: one canvas and two scroll bars, however many rows and columns the model has.

Data comes from any GridModel, such as a list of objects (ListGridModel), a function (ComputedGridModel) or pages loaded on demand (PagedGridModel). Cells are painted by CellRenderers, chosen per cell, and styled by a CellStyleProvider. Table-wide colors, fonts and sizes are CSS properties (-grid-*), resolved once per CSS pass; the CSS reference lists them.

Rows and columns each have a view order (as shown: filtered, sorted, reordered) and a model order (as in the data). Selection, cellAt(double, double) and getCellBounds(int, int) use view indices. Configuration (widths, renderers, sorting) and the selection data methods use model indices. Convert with viewToModelRow(int), modelToViewRow(int), viewToModelColumn(int) and modelToViewColumn(int).

Columns run left to right also in right-to-left scenes.

  • Property Details

    • model

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<GridModel> modelProperty
      The data shown. Setting another model resets columns, sorting, the row filter and the selection. Style, renderer and row height providers stay.
      See Also:
      • getModel()
      • setModel(GridModel)
      • modelProperty()

    • rowFilter

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<IntPredicate> rowFilterProperty
      Shows only model rows the filter accepts, null shows all. See RowFilters and ListGridModel.matching(Predicate). Inserted rows are filtered when they arrive; rows whose values change are filtered again by refreshView(). The selection stays on the rows that are still shown (up to 100,000 selected rows, a larger selection is cleared).
      See Also:
      • getRowFilter()
      • setRowFilter(IntPredicate)
      • rowFilterProperty()

    • sortKeys

      public final javafx.beans.property.ReadOnlyObjectProperty<List<SortKey>> sortKeysProperty
      The columns the rows are sorted by, the first one decides; empty when unsorted. Changes when the user clicks a header.
      See Also:
      • getSortKeys()
      • sortKeysProperty()

    • columnGroups

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<List<ColumnGroup>> columnGroupsProperty

      Rows of column groups above the column headers, outermost first. Each ColumnGroup names the group of a model column at its level, or returns null for none. Neighbouring columns with the same names at a level and all levels above share one header cell; a column without groups further down gets a taller header. Groups are functions, so they work for any number of columns. They are only shown: columns still move one by one, and a moved column may split its group.

      grid.setColumnGroups(List.of(
        column -> column == 0 ? null : column < 3 ? "Person" : "Address",
        column -> column < 3 ? null : column < 5 ? "Street" : "Town"));
      See Also:
      • getColumnGroups()
      • setColumnGroups(List)
      • columnGroupsProperty()

    • sortable

      public final javafx.beans.property.BooleanProperty sortableProperty
      Whether a click on a column header sorts: ascending, descending, then unsorted. A plain click makes the column the only sort column, continuing from its direction if it was one of several; Shift+click adds it to the sort or changes its direction there. A double-click sorts once. When off, or in SelectionMode.COLUMN, a header click selects the column. Sorting reads every value of the column, so turn it off for huge models.
      See Also:
      • isSortable()
      • setSortable(boolean)
      • sortableProperty()

    • focusedModelRow

      public final javafx.beans.property.ReadOnlyIntegerProperty focusedModelRowProperty
      Model row of the focused cell, or -1. Follows the keyboard and the mouse, so a detail view can listen to it: grid.focusedModelRowProperty().addListener((o, old, row) -> show(people.getItem(row.intValue()))).
      See Also:
      • getFocusedModelRow()
      • focusedModelRowProperty()

      Called on double-click or Enter, unless the cell is edited in place instead.

    • cellContextMenuFactory

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<Function<GridCell, javafx.scene.control.ContextMenu>> cellContextMenuFactoryProperty

      Builds the context menu for a cell the user right-clicks, or opens the menu for with the keyboard (menu key or Shift+F10, for the focused cell). Right-clicking a cell outside the selection selects it first, so menu actions can work on getSelectedModelRows() or forEachSelectedCell(Grid.CellVisitor). Return null for no menu.

      grid.setCellContextMenuFactory(cell -> new ContextMenu(
        menuItem("Open " + cell.value(), () -> open(cell.modelRow())),
        menuItem("Delete selected rows", this::deleteSelection)));

      The column header has its own menu, see columnMenuEnabledProperty().

      See Also:
      • getCellContextMenuFactory()
      • setCellContextMenuFactory(Function)
      • cellContextMenuFactoryProperty()

    • editable

      public final javafx.beans.property.BooleanProperty editableProperty
      In-place editing, off by default; a form next to the grid is usually the better choice. When on, cells the model marks editable (GridModel.isCellEditable(int, int)) are edited on double-click, F2 or typing a character, which starts the text. Enter commits, Tab commits and edits the next cell, Escape cancels. Input that cannot be converted stays in the editor with a message that shows the old value as an example. Check boxes are not edited as text: a click on the box or Space toggles them.
      See Also:
      • isEditable()
      • setEditable(boolean)
      • editableProperty()

    • autoFitColumns

      public final javafx.beans.property.BooleanProperty autoFitColumnsProperty
      Whether columns without an explicit width fit their header and the first 50 rows, at most 320 pixels wide and within their limits. On by default. The first 100 columns are fitted when data arrives and again when fonts, padding or the header renderer change. Sorting widens a column whose header no longer fits next to the sort arrow, and opening an item of a TreeGrid widens the tree column for its children. Columns resized by the user or with GridColumn.setWidth(double) keep their width. When off, columns start 100 pixels wide.
      See Also:
      • isAutoFitColumns()
      • setAutoFitColumns(boolean)
      • autoFitColumnsProperty()

    • columnMenuEnabled

      public final javafx.beans.property.BooleanProperty columnMenuEnabledProperty
      Whether right-clicking the column header (or Alt+Down on a focused cell) opens the column menu: sort, fit, hide and show columns. On by default; columnMenuFactoryProperty() replaces or extends the menu.
      See Also:
      • isColumnMenuEnabled()
      • setColumnMenuEnabled(boolean)
      • columnMenuEnabledProperty()

    • columnMenuFactory

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<Function<GridColumn, javafx.scene.control.ContextMenu>> columnMenuFactoryProperty

      Builds the column menu, null for the built-in one. The column is null when the menu is opened right of the last column. To extend the built-in menu, start from createColumnMenu(GridColumn):

      grid.setColumnMenuFactory(column -> {
    ContextMenu menu = grid.createColumnMenu(column);
    menu.getItems().add(new MenuItem("Export"));
    return menu;
});
      See Also:

      See Also:

      • tooltipProviderProperty()

    • tooltipGraphicProvider

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<Function<GridCell, javafx.scene.Node>> tooltipGraphicProviderProperty

      A node shown in the tooltip of a cell, next to its text if it has one: a small chart, an image, a few labels. Asked once each time the mouse enters a cell; null for a cell without one. The grid's tooltips have the style class grid-tooltip, so CSS can change their look and timing, e.g. -fx-show-delay.

      grid.setTooltipGraphicProvider(cell -> new VBox(new Label(person(cell).name()), chartOf(person(cell))));
      See Also:
      • getTooltipGraphicProvider()
      • setTooltipGraphicProvider(Function)
      • tooltipGraphicProviderProperty()

    • placeholder

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<javafx.scene.Node> placeholderProperty
      Shown in the middle of the grid while it shows no rows, for example a label "No matches" for a filter that hides everything. null (the default) shows "No rows"; an empty Region shows nothing.

    • headerRenderer

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<CellRenderer> headerRendererProperty

      Paints the content of the column headers, by default the column name as text, aligned like the column's values: right above numbers, centered above booleans, left otherwise. Its context has the column name as value and row -1; font, text color and alignment come from the header style (GridColumn.setHeaderStyle(CellStyle)) or the grid's -grid-header-* properties. The grid paints the background before and the sort arrow after it. A column's own header renderer (GridColumn.setHeaderRenderer(CellRenderer)) wins.

      The renderer can look at CellContext.getModelColumn(), so one renderer serves millions of columns.

      See Also:

      • setHeaderRenderer(CellRenderer)

    • sort

      public final void sort(List<SortKey> keys)
      Sorts by model columns, stable: the first key decides, the next ones break its ties. Strings sort ignoring case unless the column has its own comparator. Inserted rows are placed in order; rows whose values change keep their place until the next sort. The selection stays on its rows (up to 100,000 selected rows), unless the model sorts itself (GridModel.sortRows(List, IntFunction)), which clears it.
      Parameters:
      keys - the model columns and directions, each column once; empty for the model order
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if a column does not exist
      IllegalArgumentException - if a column appears twice

    • columnGroupsProperty

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<List<ColumnGroup>> columnGroupsProperty()

      Rows of column groups above the column headers, outermost first. Each ColumnGroup names the group of a model column at its level, or returns null for none. Neighbouring columns with the same names at a level and all levels above share one header cell; a column without groups further down gets a taller header. Groups are functions, so they work for any number of columns. They are only shown: columns still move one by one, and a moved column may split its group.

      grid.setColumnGroups(List.of(
        column -> column == 0 ? null : column < 3 ? "Person" : "Address",
        column -> column < 3 ? null : column < 5 ? "Street" : "Town"));
      Returns:
      the columnGroups property
      See Also:
      • getColumnGroups()
      • setColumnGroups(List)

    • sortableProperty

      public final javafx.beans.property.BooleanProperty sortableProperty()
      Whether a click on a column header sorts: ascending, descending, then unsorted. A plain click makes the column the only sort column, continuing from its direction if it was one of several; Shift+click adds it to the sort or changes its direction there. A double-click sorts once. When off, or in SelectionMode.COLUMN, a header click selects the column. Sorting reads every value of the column, so turn it off for huge models.
      Returns:
      the sortable property
      See Also:

      • setSortable(boolean)

    • copySelection

      public final boolean copySelection()
      Copies the selected cells to the clipboard as tab-separated text, in view order, each cell as it is shown (the text its renderer draws). Several ranges are copied together when they span the same columns, such as rows picked with Ctrl+click, or the same rows. Returns false if nothing is selected, the ranges do not line up like that, or they hold more than 1,000,000 cells; Ctrl+C then shows a message.

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<Function<GridCell, javafx.scene.control.ContextMenu>> cellContextMenuFactoryProperty()

      Builds the context menu for a cell the user right-clicks, or opens the menu for with the keyboard (menu key or Shift+F10, for the focused cell). Right-clicking a cell outside the selection selects it first, so menu actions can work on getSelectedModelRows() or forEachSelectedCell(Grid.CellVisitor). Return null for no menu.

      grid.setCellContextMenuFactory(cell -> new ContextMenu(
        menuItem("Open " + cell.value(), () -> open(cell.modelRow())),
        menuItem("Delete selected rows", this::deleteSelection)));

    • editableProperty

      public final javafx.beans.property.BooleanProperty editableProperty()
      In-place editing, off by default; a form next to the grid is usually the better choice. When on, cells the model marks editable (GridModel.isCellEditable(int, int)) are edited on double-click, F2 or typing a character, which starts the text. Enter commits, Tab commits and edits the next cell, Escape cancels. Input that cannot be converted stays in the editor with a message that shows the old value as an example. Check boxes are not edited as text: a click on the box or Space toggles them.
      Returns:
      the editable property
      See Also:
      • isEditable()
      • setEditable(boolean)

      In-place editing, off by default; a form next to the grid is usually the better choice. When on, cells the model marks editable (GridModel.isCellEditable(int, int)) are edited on double-click, F2 or typing a character, which starts the text. Enter commits, Tab commits and edits the next cell, Escape cancels. Input that cannot be converted stays in the editor with a message that shows the old value as an example. Check boxes are not edited as text: a click on the box or Space toggles them.
      Returns:
      the value of the editable property
      See Also:
      • setEditable(boolean)
      • editableProperty()

    • autoFitColumnsProperty

      public final javafx.beans.property.BooleanProperty autoFitColumnsProperty()
      Whether columns without an explicit width fit their header and the first 50 rows, at most 320 pixels wide and within their limits. On by default. The first 100 columns are fitted when data arrives and again when fonts, padding or the header renderer change. Sorting widens a column whose header no longer fits next to the sort arrow, and opening an item of a TreeGrid widens the tree column for its children. Columns resized by the user or with GridColumn.setWidth(double) keep their width. When off, columns start 100 pixels wide.
      Returns:
      the autoFitColumns property
      See Also:
      • isAutoFitColumns()
      • setAutoFitColumns(boolean)

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<Function<GridCell, javafx.scene.Node>> tooltipGraphicProviderProperty()

    • setLayout

      public final void setLayout(GridLayout layout)
      Restores an arrangement from getLayout(), as far as it fits the current columns: a column with another name at its index is found by name or left out, columns the layout does not know keep their defaults and come last, and the column order is used only if its columns kept their names. Frozen columns and zoom are kept within their limits. Clears the selection. Does nothing for null, which GridLayout.decode(String) returns for blank text.

    • setDefaultRenderer

      public final void setDefaultRenderer(Class<?> type, CellRenderer renderer)
      Renderer for all columns whose GridModel.getColumnClass(int) is type, a subclass or an implementation of it, and in columns of mixed types (Object.class) for every value of such a class. The nearest class wins, then the nearest interface; primitive column classes count as their wrappers. Built in: numbers right aligned, booleans as check boxes, everything else as text.
      Parameters:
      type - the class, superclass or interface
      renderer - its renderer

    • headerRendererProperty

      public final javafx.beans.property.ObjectProperty<CellRenderer> headerRendererProperty()

      Paints the content of the column headers, by default the column name as text, aligned like the column's values: right above numbers, centered above booleans, left otherwise. Its context has the column name as value and row -1; font, text color and alignment come from the header style (GridColumn.setHeaderStyle(CellStyle)) or the grid's -grid-header-* properties. The grid paints the background before and the sort arrow after it. A column's own header renderer (GridColumn.setHeaderRenderer(CellRenderer)) wins.

      The renderer can look at CellContext.getModelColumn(), so one renderer serves millions of columns.

      Returns:
      the headerRenderer property
      See Also:
      • getHeaderRenderer()
      • setHeaderRenderer(CellRenderer)

      public final void scrollTo(int viewRow, int viewColumn)
      Scrolls as little as possible to show a view cell fully. It scrolls in the next layout pass, so it also works before the grid is shown and right after rows were added. For a model row or column, convert with modelToViewRow(int) and modelToViewColumn(int).
      Parameters:

      viewColumn - the view column
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if the grid does not show that cell
